title: Director, Venture Cafe London
description: Are you a natural leader with a strong network, driven to tackle your city's biggest challenges and connect diverse groups to make things happen? If so, you belong at Venture Café! At Venture Café, we aim to create a global community of innovators with equal access to resources and opportunities, addressing our most pressing challenges. Ready to make an impact with us? The Venture Café Global Institute (VCGI) seeks a strategic, dynamic, and self-driven Director to lead Venture Café London in the heart of the Knowledge Quarter. This is a unique opportunity to operate and grow a hub for Deeptech innovation and connection, in close collaboration with ARIA . ABOUT VENTURE CAFÉ Venture Café believes that Isolation is the enemy of innovation and our mission is clear: Connect innovators to make things happen. We are a neutral and trusted center of gravity that connects the entire innovation ecosystem and is available for everyone. Our flagship program, the Thursday Gathering, is a dynamic and intentionally designed experience freely accessible to all. Featuring vibrant networking sessions activated with captivating demos or immersion in the night’s theme by attending thought-provoking sessions led by inspiring speakers. Here, curiosity meets opportunity, connections flourish, and innovation thrives. Venture Café was founded by Tim Rowe, founder and CEO of the Cambridge Innovation Center (CIC), in 2009 and helped fuel the growth of one of the world’s most powerful innovation ecosystems: Boston’s Kendall Square. What began with a modest gathering of 12 people at our inaugural Thursday Gathering has flourished into the Venture Café Global Institute (VCGI). Over the past 15 years, VCGI has united over 900,000 visionaries, developers, creatives, and civic leaders across 24cities worldwide, building a global community of communities. At VCGI, we believe if we’re going to solve humankind’s biggest challenges, we need as many amazing humans as possible involved in that process. YOUR DAY-TO-DAY WORK Reporting to the Head of UK, Venture Cafe United Kingdom, you will lead the established Venture Café London team, directing programming for the Thursday Gathering and other ecosystem-building activities. Your goal is to ensure Venture Café programming continues to connect local innovators to the national and international entrepreneurship community. Your role would be to execute weekly Venture Café Thursday Gatherings including the following: • Collaborating closely with VCGI and ARIA to continue to successfully implement and refine the strategy for Venture Café London. • Scoping and securing financial partners for Venture Café London and building a pipeline for funding opportunities. • Working closely with the Head of UK and the other UK Directors to ensure success and align initiatives where appropriate. • Scoping and developing a rolling programming strategy to inspire and connect the local innovation community. • Collaborate with the ARIA team and Programme Directors to drive value to the ARIA Opportunity Spaces. • Identifying and partnering with local ecosystem leaders as an advocate and spokesperson to build diverse and inclusive programs. • Developing innovative program formats for delivering content and creating connection opportunities to maximize engagement. • Leading and overseeing strategic planning, impact measurement and program budget for Venture Café in London. • Attracting sponsorship for programs and aligning them within the Thursday Gathering framework. • L eading and coaching your three direct reports towards success. • Continuously reviewing and implementing improvements/changes to ensure the ongoing success and reputation of Venture Café London. • Collaborating with the Venture Café global network and ARIA to connect the London community to global opportunities. • Identifying and mitigating risks to the effective operation of the Thursday Gathering. • Nurturing existing initiatives to support Venture Café’s Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging (DEIB) efforts, while bringing a visionary approach to developing and expanding DEIB-driven programming and partnership opportunities. ABOUT YOU You understand your city’s challenges and see them as opportunities, combining a fascination with trends and a humanistic perspective. Passionate about mission-driven work, you'll lead Venture Café London by nurturing relationships, leading teams, and thriving in ambiguity. Your skills include leading programs, matchmaking, innovating, connecting with the community, and fostering collaboration. You are comfortable with public speaking, have excellent communication skills, and excel at connecting across business, academia, government, and civil society. You bring a global outlook with local roots and a strong community commitment. ​​More specifically, you thrive in: • Leading people and complex programs. • Being a match-maker extraordinaire and seeing opportunities at the intersections of people, ideas & resources. • Envisioning, developing and implementing innovative program experiences. • Connecting with a broad cross-section of the community. • Bringing people together to collaborate towards a common goal. • Identifying and developing mutually beneficial partnerships. Additionally, you have: • Knowledge of London’s startup community, key influencers, networks and organizations. • Excellent organizational, project, and task management skills. • Experience securing funding opportunities and a network of potential funders. • Comfort in Google Suite, email campaign software, and project management software. • Fluency in English. • Ability to legally work in the UK. We are unable to sponsor visas for this role at this time. OUR OFFER • Employment contract. • Competitive compensation based on experience • 4% Pension Contribution • 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays • Supplemental medical and dental insurance • £200 Monthly Commuter Allowance • Life insurance • Business Travel Insurance • Hybrid work model – You will work three days per week in the office, with Thursdays required as a core in-office day. VENTURE CAFÉ LONDON - GUIDING ORGANIZATIONAL OBJECTIVES As an organization, Venture Café London is guided by five core objectives that shape how success is measured. These objectives are advanced through purposeful programming, storytelling, and bringing together a diverse community of innovators, entrepreneurs, investors, researchers, corporates, and ecosystem partners. Broaden access to innovation and economic opportunity. Lower barriers to entry and create an inclusive, welcoming environment where people from diverse backgrounds can participate in and contribute to London's innovation ecosystem. Connect people and break down silos. Build bridges across sectors, disciplines, industries, and communities to encourage collaboration, knowledge sharing, and the development of a globally competitive innovation ecosystem. Improve access to resources and opportunities. Foster meaningful relationships that connect innovators and entrepreneurs with the capital, talent, expertise, ideas, and strategic partnerships they need to develop and scale their ventures. Create spaces for meaningful human connection. Bring people together through accessible, engaging experiences that encourage the exchange of ideas, build trust, and turn spontaneous interactions into lasting relationships and collaborations. Strengthen the wider innovation ecosystem through shared resources. Openly share knowledge, tools, and opportunities while collaborating with ecosystem partners to align efforts, amplify impact, and support collective progress. The Venture Café Gathering The flagship Venture Café model is the weekly Gathering: a recurring community event where innovators, entrepreneurs, investors, researchers, and other ecosystem stakeholders come together to exchange ideas, share knowledge, explore emerging technologies, and build meaningful connections. Through expert-led discussions, educational sessions, networking opportunities, and informal interactions, the Gathering creates the conditions for collaboration and new opportunities to emerge organically. It serves as a platform for connecting London's innovation community and provides a foundation for wider programming, strategic partnerships, and ecosystem-building initiatives. The Gathering is more than an event; it is a recurring platform for strengthening relationships across the innovation ecosystem and helping promising ideas develop into meaningful collaborations and real-world outcomes. title: Senior Digital Activation Executive | Lookfantastic
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">About THG</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":0,"335559739":160,"335559740":279}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">We are THG, a global ecommerce group on a mission to be the global online leader in beauty and sports nutrition.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Our portfolio of</span><span data-contrast="auto"> leading retailers and brands such as LOOKFANTASTIC, Myprotein, ESPA, Perricone MD, and Cult Beauty form our two core businesses: THG Beauty and THG Nutrition.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">From Manchester to New York, we’re powered by a team of over 2500 people who work together, lead by example, and think BIG. </span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">With us, you’ll go further, faster. What are you waiting for?</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p></div><h3><strong>Life at THG Beauty </strong></h3> <p>We know that beauty isn’t one-size-fits-all. Our portfolio of leading retailers and iconic beauty brands caters to everyone, everywhere, empowering customers all over the world to look and feel fantastic.</p> <p>By combining our portfolio of owned brands inclusive of ESPA, Ameliorate and Christophe Robin, with a marketplace for over 1,300 third-party beauty brands through online retail sites LOOKFANTASTIC, Cult Beauty, and Dermstore, THG Beauty's ambition is to be the global digital partner of choice across the beauty industry, supporting the channel shift to online.</p> <p>THG Beauty’s breadth of relationships is unique to the beauty market; it engages with brands as a retailer, a brand owner, and a product developer and manufacturer, making it the industry’s digital strategic leader. </p> <h3><strong><span data-contrast="auto">Why be a Senior Digital Activation Executive at LOOKFANTASTIC?</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":0,"335559739":160,"335559740":279}"> </span></h3> <p data-pm-slice="1 3 []">The Senior Digital Activation Executive role sits within THG Beauty's Retail Media structure, working closely with brand marketing leads, buying, trading, performance marketing and creative teams to deliver impactful, brand-funded media campaigns.</p> <p>This is a hands-on digital activation role, combining platform expertise, campaign execution and performance analysis with brand-facing relationship management. You'll play a key role in bringing media plans to life across platforms such as Meta and TikTok, monitoring performance, making data-led optimisations and reporting on campaign success.</p> <p>You'll act as an external-facing LOOKFANTASTIC ambassador and media specialist, building relationships with our brand partners and helping them maximise their investment through effective digital activation.</p> <p>As a <strong>Senior Digital Activation Executive</strong>, you'll:</p> <ul> <li>Build strong relationships with LOOKFANTASTIC's key brand partners, understanding their objectives and developing data-driven paid media strategies to drive brand growth.</li> <li>Develop, pitch and activate multi-platform digital media plans across relevant paid social and digital advertising channels.</li> <li>Take hands-on ownership of campaign activation across platforms, including Meta Business Manager and TikTok Ads Manager, managing campaign set-up, implementation and ongoing performance.</li> <li>Monitor live campaign performance, proactively identifying opportunities to optimise targeting, creative, budgets and delivery against agreed KPIs and ROI targets.</li> <li>Own mid-campaign and post-campaign reporting, analysing performance data, identifying key insights and demonstrating campaign uplift and return on investment.</li> <li>Translate campaign data into clear, actionable recommendations for brand partners, helping shape future media strategies and secure incremental investment.</li> <li>Work collaboratively with our influencer team to commission high-quality influencer assets for paid media repurposing.</li> <li>Support social-first creative and ad copy development, briefing our in-house creative team to deliver engaging, high-performing assets.</li> <li>Work closely with wider marketing, e-commerce, buying and trading teams to ensure campaigns are aligned with wider commercial objectives.</li> <li>Keep up to date with emerging digital platforms, advertising features and industry trends, bringing new ideas and opportunities to improve campaign performance.</li> </ul> <p><strong><span data-contrast="auto">What skills and experience do I need for this role?</span></strong><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":0,"335559739":160,"335559740":279}"> </span></p> <ul> <li>2+ years' experience in paid media, digital marketing or digital campaign activation.</li> <li><strong>Hands-on experience with paid media platforms</strong>, ideally Meta Business Manager and TikTok Ads Manager, with confidence setting up, managing and optimising campaigns.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret campaign data, monitor KPIs and produce meaningful performance reports.</li> <li>A commercial mindset, understanding how to use media investment effectively to drive performance, growth and ROI.</li> <li>Confidence working with campaign budgets, targeting, creative testing and optimisation.</li> <li>Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships and confidently present campaign recommendations to external brand partners.</li> <li>A proactive, digitally savvy individual who naturally keeps up with emerging platforms, social trends and developments in the paid media landscape.</li> <li>Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple campaigns and deadlines.</li> <li>A passion for beauty, e-commerce and the evolving retail media industry.</li> </ul> <p><span title: Engineering Director
description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Join Axon and be a Force for Good.</strong></h4> <p>At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.<br><br>Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.</p></div><h2>About Axon</h2> <p>Axon’s mission is bold and simple: Protect Life. We build technology that gives first responders, enterprises and communities the clarity to act in the moments that matter most.</p> <p>Our Real-Time Operations (RTO) portfolio, powered by Fusus, is transforming how public safety and security organisations detect, assess and respond to incidents. By connecting live video, devices and operational systems, we help customers build a shared understanding of what is happening—and respond with greater confidence.</p> <p>We’re looking for a Director of Software Engineering to help build and scale the mission-critical software behind these experiences.</p> <h2>The Role</h2> <p>As Director of Software Engineering within Real-Time Operations, you will lead multiple engineering teams delivering secure, reliable and scalable software for public safety and enterprise customers.</p> <p>You will own the technical direction and engineering execution for your area, translating product priorities into clear plans and measurable outcomes. Working closely with Product, Design and other engineering leaders, you will guide architectural decisions, develop engineering talent and ensure teams deliver software that customers can depend on.</p> <p>This role requires a leader who combines technical depth with strong people leadership. You will be comfortable moving between long-term strategy and delivery detail—challenging assumptions, making trade-offs and creating the conditions for teams to do their best work.</p> <h2>Your Impact</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Deliver technology that matters.</strong> Lead teams building software that supports real-time situational awareness and incident response.</li> <li><strong>Shape technical direction.</strong> Establish a clear technical strategy that balances customer needs, platform reuse and long-term maintainability.</li> <li><strong>Build strong teams.</strong> Develop engineering managers and technical leaders, strengthening ownership, collaboration and accountability.</li> <li><strong>Raise engineering standards.</strong> Improve reliability, security and delivery quality across systems that span devices, cloud services and user-facing applications.</li> <li><strong>Connect strategy to execution.</strong> Partner with Product and Design to turn customer problems into prioritised roadmaps and dependable delivery.</li> </ul> <h2>What You’ll Do</h2> <p><strong>Reports to: </strong>VP, Software Engineering</p> <p><strong>Work Location:</strong> This role is based out of our London office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.</p> <p><strong>Role & Responsibilities:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead and develop multiple software engineering teams, setting clear expectations for technical quality, delivery and team performance.</li> <li>Partner with Product and Design to define roadmaps, sequence investments and make informed trade-offs between new capabilities, platform improvements and technical debt.</li> <li>Guide architecture and system-design decisions across your description: The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. We're looking for candidates based in either London or Leeds. The role iwoca's Financial Crime Analysts protect our customers and our business from fraud. You'll become an expert in how fraudsters target small businesses and card products, helping our business credit card grow safely while keeping the experience smooth for genuine customers. You'll investigate suspicious applications, accounts and card activity, owning the process from first alert to final decision. Working closely with our Credit Cards and Operations teams, you'll spot new fraud patterns early to help strengthen our controls. From time to time, you'll also support our core lending business with fraud cases on our Flexi-Loan, giving you a wider view of financial crime across iwoca. Your mission will be: Investigating cases flagged as a potential fraud or AML risk. Including CIFAS flags, facial biometric anomalies, device based anomalies, signs of document tampering and more. Screening PEP, sanction and adverse media matches. Taking ownership of customer verification on a case by case basis and deciding what information is required to reduce the risk of fraud and money laundering. Monitoring account activity and transactions, investigating anything unusual and raising unusual activity where needed. Identifying opportunities to improve our processes and implement changes which will make us more efficient Working closely with our Account Managers, Credit Analyst and Broker teams to maintain our high fraud prevention standards while ensuring a fast and slick service. The requirements We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve. Ideally, you’ll have: At least 1 years’ experience within a financial crime related role Good knowledge of fraud and financial crime Brilliant communication skills and experience delivering constructive and candid feedback A confident and enthusiastic attitude that works well in a regularly changing and fast-paced environment A pragmatic, risk-based approach to case investigation An analytical mindset with a practical approach to problem solving, sometimes we need to make decisions with limited information Whilst we welcome applications from all qualified candidates, please note that this particular position does not offer visa sponsorship. Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK independently. The salary Our base salary range in Leeds is £30,000 - £35,000 and our base salary range in London is £35,000 - £40,000. We want to pay all of our employees fairly, so that’s why we regularly benchmark salaries based on market rates and to recognise your increasing value to our business. The culture At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time. The offices We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work: Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks. Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions. The benefits Flexible working hours. Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership. A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses. A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents. 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave. A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years. Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support. 3% Pension contributions on total earnings. An employee equity incentive scheme. Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money. Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme. Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield. And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer: A learning and development budget for everyone. Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers. Access to learning platforms like Treehouse. description: Staff Backend Engineer - Ledger Platform Hybrid in London, UK We’re looking for a Staff Backend Engineer to join the Ledger Platform team. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. The team The Ledger Platform team is rebuilding all of iwoca’s ledgers as one platform, starting with the ledger for the business credit card. Every card payment, loan repayment, and payout will end up there. Finance, Accounting, and Capital Markets rely on that record, so it has to be right every time. The team is small – a principal engineer who leads it, another staff engineer, another engineer, and you. It works closely with the product teams that build on its ledgers, and with Finance. The role You'll lead projects from design to production, and decide with product what the team builds and how. With the principal engineer, you’ll set the platform’s technical direction, from service boundaries to the APIs and event streams other teams build on. Most of the platform is still to be built, and you’ll own part of it yourself. It’s a hands-on individual contributor role with high ownership and no line management. Every payment a small business makes with iwoca crosses several services and network hops before it reaches the ledger, and any of them can fail. You'll build services that record each one exactly once, with no single point of failure, safe timeouts and retries, and graceful degradation when a dependency is down. When something breaks in production, you'll fix it so it doesn't break again. You’ll learn iwoca’s financial products in depth, so you can challenge requirements and explain technical trade-offs to Finance. When the answer isn’t obvious, you’ll scope and prototype, and use domain modelling to find the simple design behind a complicated problem. Building the ledgers for Flexi-Loan and iwocaPay. Account migration. Moving existing loan accounts onto the new ledgers with zero downtime and no data lost. Credit card ledger. Building new features for the credit card ledger, from real-time card holds to daily interest and monthly statements. Reconciliation and journals. Reconciling the ledger with banks, payment providers, and the card scheme, and producing the accounting journals Finance relies on. Funding facilities. Recording how loans move between iwoca’s funding facilities. The requirements Essential: Distributed systems. You’ve built and run fault-tolerant services in production, and handled the hard parts: durable communication between services, idempotency, transactional correctness, and partial failure. You’ve worked in depth with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, and solved data integrity, concurrency, and performance problems in them. Ownership. You’ve led large projects across several engineers or teams, end to end, and helped other engineers grow through design and code reviews. Testing. You’ve tested for edge cases and failures as carefully as you designed for them. AI leverage. You’ve built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production. Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience. Bonus: Financial systems. You’ve built ledgers, billing, or payment systems, including the audit trails and reconciliation that prove they’re correct. High volume. You’ve worked at a company where the volume of data or transactions shaped how you designed systems. Migrations. You’ve moved live systems and data onto a new platform with zero downtime. Python. You’ve used Python in production, with a web framework such as Django, FastAPI, or Flask. You will be expected to move programs forward with incomplete information, surface and resolve gaps before they become blockers, and hold multiple workstreams accountable across time zones and organizational boundaries. The best candidates bring deep experience at the intersection of data center construction handover and AI/GPU hardware deployment. You know how construction sequences impact infrastructure readiness, how ICT and CDU work intersect, and how to drive multi-threaded bring-up programs spanning hardware, networking, power, and cooling. What You'll Do Program Delivery & Execution Own end-to-end delivery of GPU cluster activations and data center infrastructure programs, from initial strategic planning through operational handoff. Drive multi-threaded bring-up programs spanning hardware, networking, power, and cooling — owning plans, dependencies, and critical paths. Coordinate cross-functional teams responsible for construction, infrastructure, network, hardware, ICT, commissioning, and operations, including vendor and contractor partners. Anticipate downstream impacts of technical sequencing decisions on capacity, schedule, and cluster performance; identify and resolve blockers before they surface. Manage and hold accountable vendors, integration contractors, and third-party service providers across the full deployment lifecycle. Partner with engineering to improve cluster turn-up reliability, repeatability, and automation — reducing time-to-serve for new capacity. Support network operations and end-to-end physical and logical bring-up, including on-site deployment, rack cabling, and coordination with engineering teams. Maintain momentum through changing requirements, tight timelines, and cross-time-zone execution. Stakeholder & Executive Communication Influence senior executive and c-suite strategic approaches. Deliver crisp executive-level program status briefings covering schedule health, risks, key decisions, and escalation paths across a broad portfolio of concurrent programs. Translate complex technical requirements — from highly detailed customer RFPs, integration specs, and architecture documents — into actionable plans for engineering, finance, and marketing stakeholders. Serve as the primary cross-functional point of contact between engineering, operations, customers, and leadership; code-switch fluently between deeply technical and business-facing audiences. Interface with chip and hardware providers to derisk onboarding to new platforms across compute, networking, and cooling stacks. Facilitate alignment across stakeholders at all levels — from network engineers to C-suite — with confidence, clarity, and no ego. Program Infrastructure & Process Build and operationalize program mechanisms — roadmaps, milestones, risk registers, RACI matrices, decision logs, and deployment runbooks — that make delivery predictable at scale. Establish and maintain a single source of truth for all active programs using tools such as Smartsheet, Confluence, Jira, and Notion. Identify bottlenecks and systemic gaps, then drive durable fixes across tooling, process, and partner interfaces. Develop scalable playbooks and governance frameworks that create accountability without creating overhead as Volta's deployment footprint grows rapidly. Champion automation and digital workflows to eliminate manual effort across the program lifecycle. What You'll Bring Required 5+ years of experience delivering complex data center physical infrastructure programs or large-scale GPU/AI cluster deployments in fast-moving environments. description: About Volta Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. About the role Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for frontier AI customers. Growing this fast produces a long tail of manual internal work: invoices retyped into banking portals, expense reports chased by hand, spreadsheets reconciled every month, accounts provisioned ticket by ticket. Each task is small. Together they cost the company real time, and they multiply with every new sit and every new hire. This role removes that work permanently. You sit with the person who owns a process, understand what it actually does, then build the integration that runs it against banking and accounting systems, Microsoft Graph / Office, Slack, Jira and Confluence, and the HR and identity stack. Most of the answer is well built API code with sound authentication, error handling, escalation, audibility and observability. Some of it uses models, for classification, extraction, or matching, where that is the right tool rather than the fashionable one. Knowing the difference is a large part of the job. Much of this work lands inside the financial reporting path, and Volta is building toward SOX compliance alongside its existing ISO 27001 and SOC 2 obligations. An automation that touches invoices, payments, or reconciliation becomes part of the control environment the moment it goes live. That sets the bar: changes are reviewed, tested, and traceable, access is least privilege and segregated, every run leaves an audit trail an external auditor can follow, and nobody moves code into production by hand. You build to that standard from the first commit rather than retrofitting it under deadline. Regulation shapes the work in a second way. Volta is headquartered in the UK and operates across the EU, so anything you build with AI in it sits under the EU AI Act as well as UK and EU data protection law. Automation that touches hiring, performance, or other employment decisions carries the heaviest obligations, and the line between a helpful classifier and a regulated decision system is easy to cross without noticing. You are expected to recognize where that line runs, keep a person in the loop where the law requires one, document what you deploy, and bring Legal and Security in early rather than after the build. You sit inside Corporate IT at a fast-growing AI-forward company, which owns the tooling, accounts, and API access you build on, and which gives you engineers next to you for design discussion and code review rather than leaving you to mark your own homework. Security Engineering advises on access and compliance. The first internal customer is the accounting and finance team. After that the scope is the whole company: finance, IT, People, delivery, product, and the engineering teams for their own internal overhead. Very little here is customer facing. Initially, you are the only person doing this work full time, so you prioritize hard, ship small, and build things that keep running without you next to them. Keep a human decision point where a control requires one Build agentic automations where a single scripted path will not hold: an agent that picks up a case, calls the tools it needs across Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian and the finance stack, and stops at a human approval gate before anything with money or access impact. Internal systems arrive in whatever language, runtime, and SDK their vendor picked, and you are expected to work in what the problem needs rather than bending every problem toward one stack. title: Eco Toxicologist Risk Assessment Consultant
description: About 3E: 3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions. You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges. Join us and make an impact! About Yordas 3E, the leading global provider of expert-led AI compliance solutions for chemical and workplace safety, product stewardship, and sustainable supply chains, recently acquired Yordas Group, a leading international provider of scientific consulting and regulatory content services across chemical management, sustainability, and regulatory compliance. Headquartered in Lancaster, UK, with operations in Germany, Canada, Turkey, and Japan, Yordas serves global brands through its Scientific Services, Regulatory Intelligence, Product Compliance, and Hazard Communication offerings. About the Role Understanding the potential impact of chemicals on human health and the environment is essential to helping businesses develop safer products and meet evolving regulatory requirements. At Yordas, recently acquired by 3E, you'll have the opportunity to apply your scientific expertise to complex regulatory challenges while contributing to the growth of our risk assessment services. We're looking for an (Eco)toxicologist / Risk Assessment Expert to join our expanding regulatory and scientific consultancy business. In this role, you'll help clients navigate chemical safety requirements across REACH, Biocidal Products Regulation (BPR), and Cosmetics Regulations, providing the scientific insight needed to assess hazards, evaluate exposure, and manage risk. You'll collaborate with toxicologists, human health experts, chemists, external research partners, and clients to deliver high-quality scientific assessments and regulatory guidance. Beyond the technical work, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to the development of our risk assessment services across chemicals, biocides, cosmetics, medical devices, and food contact materials. This opportunity is well suited to someone who enjoys translating complex science into practical recommendations, working across disciplines, and applying their expertise to a diverse range of regulatory and product safety challenges. What You'll Do Evaluate chemical and product safety: Conduct toxicological and ecotoxicological assessments to evaluate potential risks to human health and the environment under REACH, BPR, and Cosmetics Regulations. Apply scientific modeling to real-world challenges: Perform quantitative exposure and risk assessments using tools such as CHESAR and other simulation models to evaluate human and environmental exposure. Translate scientific data into regulatory insight: Review and interpret toxicological studies, hazard information, regulatory guidance, and applicable legislation to develop scientifically sound risk assessments. Deliver high-quality regulatory reports: Prepare chemical safety reports that clearly communicate assessment methodologies, scientific findings, and risk characterization to support regulatory compliance. Coordinate external scientific studies: Commission and oversee physicochemical and environmental fate studies conducted by Contract Research Organizations (CROs), ensuring technical quality and timely delivery. Collaborate across scientific disciplines: Work closely with toxicologists, chemists, human health specialists, and other technical experts to develop comprehensive assessments and client deliverables. Provide trusted technical guidance: Communicate scientific findings, support technical positions on behalf of clients, and engage with regulatory authorities and other stakeholders on chemical safety matters. Contribute to service development: Support the continued growth of Yordas' risk assessment services across REACH, biocides, cosmetics, medical devices, and food contact regulations. Stay connected to evolving science and regulation: Participate in relevant seminars, workshops, training, and professional forums to maintain current knowledge of regulatory toxicology and risk assessment approaches. What Makes You a Great Fit We're looking for someone who brings scientific curiosity, technical expertise, and a collaborative approach to solving complex chemical safety challenges. Required Qualifications and Experience An MSc, PharmD, or PhD in Biology, Environmental Science, Health Science, or a related field, or significant practical experience in toxicological hazard and risk assessment of chemicals. Knowledge of CHESAR and other exposure modeling and risk assessment tools. A solid understanding of regulatory toxicology, particularly chemical hazard identification, exposure assessment, and risk characterization. Working knowledge of chemical hazard classification under CLP or GHS, as well as REACH regulatory requirements. A proactive, self-directed approach to work, with the ability to take ownership of technical activities and contribute effectively to a global team. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to engage with colleagues and stakeholders across different scientific disciplines. Nice to Have Approximately 2–3 years of experience working in regulatory consultancy. Familiarity with IUCLID and its application in chemical regulatory submissions. Working knowledge of additional regulatory frameworks, including the EU Biocidal Products Regulation, Cosmetics Regulations, Medical Devices Regulations, or Food Contact Regulations. Experience communicating complex scientific and regulatory information clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences. Knowledge of endocrine disruptor assessment criteria, including their application to substances such as Bisphenol A (BPA). Benefits Depending on location, employees may have access to a range of benefits, including: Pension scheme and medical benefits Generous holiday allowance Professional development opportunities Social and team activities Flexible working arrangements Interested in making an impact? If you're passionate about applying science to real-world challenges, advancing chemical safety, and helping organizations navigate complex regulatory requirements, we'd welcome your application. title: Engineering Manager
description: TrustFlight builds software that aviation operators around the world rely on to keep flying safe, for an international customer base with an unusually varied set of problems. This role exists to build and sustain a high-performing team of six to eight engineers: coaching each individual, holding a consistent standard of performance, and owning the process, testing, tooling and infrastructure the team depends on. It is a people and systems leadership role rather than a technical leadership one. Product and the technical leads decide what gets built and how; the Engineering Manager owns the conditions that allow them to build it well and quickly. The postholder is one of four Engineering Managers in a Product, Design and Engineering department of around 40 to 50 people, which is growing and maturing quickly. There is considerable scope here to shape how engineering works across it. Key Responsibilities: Raise the performance bar with every hire and every promotion. Treat coaching as a core duty of the role, and upskilling as a standing remit: develop engineers through regular 1:1s, direct feedback, stretch assignments and explicit development plans, and grow technical leads as well as individual contributors. Manage performance fairly and decisively. Set explicit expectations, recognise strong work, raise problems early and allow runway to respond, and address sustained underperformance promptly. Act as the chief unblocker for the team across tooling, infrastructure, testing and process, and own the team's infrastructure-as-code estate. Identify the genuine constraints on throughput, including code review latency, slow or flaky tests, handoffs, approval gates and unreliable environments. Remove them, ensure the team can build, test, deploy, observe and recover quickly and safely, and evidence the improvement in flow metrics. Own testing standards and the consistency of quality across the team, including the definition of “tested”, the criteria that gate a release, and the management of coverage and test flakiness. Quality should not vary according to who wrote the code. Architect cross-team developer tooling and drive consolidation of the technology estate, jointly with peer Engineering Managers and the Director of Engineering. Build the case for moving from a varied stack onto fewer, better-supported technologies. Establish paved roads and automated guardrails that teams adopt on merit, and sequence the change so that it strengthens delivery. Work with the technical leads to maintain an accurate and current picture of technical debt, quality and process constraints. Translate it into risks and opportunities the Product Manager can prioritise, so that the balance between product output and technical excellence is a deliberate decision. Lead the team's adoption of AI-assisted development. Set the standards for where and how AI is used, ensure AI-generated code is understood and accountable to a named engineer, guard against data, licensing and security risk, and maintain an evidence-based view of its effect on the team. Help establish consistent engineering practice across TrustFlight with the other Engineering Managers. No shared approach to levelling, calibration, feedback and hiring yet exists, and building one is part of this role, so that an engineer's experience does not depend on which manager they report to. Required Qualifications & Experience: At least three years' experience as a dedicated people manager of software engineers, including senior engineers and, ideally, technical leads. A software engineering background sufficient to contribute credibly in a design review, challenge an architectural decision on its merits, and distinguish a team that feels fast from one that is fast. The postholder will not act as the team's technical lead and will not be assessed on code they write. Current, practical familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD and automated testing, covering Terraform, Pulumi or equivalent, containerised deployment and a major cloud platform, sufficient to own the estate, set standards and review the work. A track record of raising and holding a quality bar across a team: testing strategy, review standards, and the discipline to keep them consistent as the team and the codebase change. Demonstrable experience of improving how a team works, supported by evidence of the resulting difference. Direct experience of performance management, including at least one case of successfully improving, or fairly exiting, an underperformer. Desirable Skills & Experience Practical experience of agentic development setups, using tools such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, introduced at team or organisation level along with the governance around them. Experience building or operating auditable agent orchestration systems. A strong advantage, though not a requirement. A track record of putting AI workflows into real use, and of helping ship AI features in production applications. An understanding that this field is changing quickly, with the adaptability to keep pace and the credibility to bring a team along on that journey. Experience leading, or contributing materially to, a technology-stack consolidation across multiple teams. Experience raising standards across a heterogeneous or inherited technology estate without mandating uniformity. Experience in a regulated, safety-critical or externally audited software environment, such as aviation, medical, defence or financial services. Valuable, though not a requirement. AI & Digital Competency TrustFlight is an AI-first organisation. Every role is expected to actively engage with AI tools and digital ways of working to drive efficiency, quality, and innovation. Tier 3 — AI Builder Develops and integrates AI-powered solutions Builds, fine-tunes, or integrates AI/ML models and pipelines. Establishes evaluation frameworks for AI systems. Ensures responsible AI practices (fairness, transparency, data governance). Contributes to TrustFlight’s AI strategy. Role-Specific AI & Digital Skills: Set and maintain the team's standards for AI-assisted development, covering which tools are approved, where they may and may not be used, and how their output is reviewed. Ensure AI-generated code entering the codebase is understood and accountable to a named engineer, and that review capacity scales with the volume AI produces. Apply AI to strengthen testing and documentation, ensuring that AI-written tests validate the requirement and do not simply confirm the behaviour of the implementation. Establish guardrails against the specific risks of AI-assisted engineering: leakage of customer or regulated data into model context, licensing contamination, and plausible but incorrect code in safety-relevant paths. AI Development & Growth Complete TrustFlight's AI fluency onboarding within the first 30 days. Dedicate time each month to evaluating emerging AI development tooling and agentic workflows, and pilot promising tools in a controlled way. Share findings with the Engineering Manager group and the wider engineering team, including negative results. Contribute to TrustFlight's engineering-wide standards for AI-assisted development, and to the evidence base available to customers and auditors. Competencies & Behaviours: People Leadership — Raises the bar with every hire and promotion; coaches deliberately and develops leaders as well as engineers; creates the conditions for people to do their best work. Fairness and Consistency — Applies the same bar and the same care to everyone; makes reasoning visible; is trusted by engineers and by peers in calibration. Systems Thinking — Treats delivery problems as problems with the system rather than with the people; identifies the constraint before asking for more effort; takes obstacles off other people's desks and measures success by the team's output. Technical Judgement — Sufficient depth to ask the right question, weigh a trade-off, and defer to the technical leads when appropriate. High Standards in a Safety Domain — Holds a consistent quality bar and does not allow defects to pass down the line; recognises that operators' safety cases depend on this software. Working Arrangements: Working Hours: 40 hours per week Work Pattern: Hybrid. London-based, with a minimum of two days per week in the London office and the remainder flexible. Travel Requirements: Occasional travel to other TrustFlight locations and to team or company events. Not a regular requirement of the role. On-Call / Shift Work: Not part of the on-call rota. Accountable for the team’s on-call practice being sustainable and fairly shared. Special Conditions: Right to work in the UK. description: <p> </p> <h2>About Fospha</h2> <p>Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on. Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, and Lululemon use Fospha every day to decide where budget should move next. title: Senior Creative Technologist, AI
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2 class="job-details__description-header text-color-secondary font-family-secondary" data-bind="i18n: 'job-details.employer-description-title'">About Us</h2> <div class="job-details__description-content basic-formatter" data-bind="html: pageData().job.corporateDescription"> <p>Fanatics is a leading global sports platform redefining how fans connect with the teams, players and moments they love. Our businesses — Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, Fanatics Betting & Gaming, Fanatics Events, Fanatics Advertising, Fanatics Markets and Fanatics Studios — maximize the presence and reach for hundreds of partners globally and create a one-stop experience that allows fans to buy, bet, collect, and earn, while engaging with sports in deeper, more immersive ways. This includes licensed fan gear and lifestyle products, sportsbook and iGaming, physical and digital trading cards, live events, premium sports entertainment content, credit card offerings and more. Together, they form a powerful, integrated ecosystem — connected by the Fanatics ONE loyalty program and FanCash, the currency of sport — delivering personalized experiences to over 100 million fans worldwide. Fanatics holds partnerships with over 900 sports properties, from professional leagues and players’ associations to teams, colleges and retail partners; over 7,000 athletes and celebrities; and over 2,000 retail locations, including all Lids stores. Backed by a team of more than 22,000 employees, Fanatics is committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience.</p> </div> <p> </p></div><h3><strong>The role</strong></h3> <p>This is a hybrid role: a designer who builds, or an engineer who designs. You have the eye to know what good looks like and the code to make it repeatable. You build and run the automated workstreams that Fanatics Casino, and the teams around it, produce brand-safe creative from every day: template and variant generators, image and video generation with our rules built in, copy-to-layout pipelines, Figma plugins.</p> <p>The stack is already here: a shared Figma design system, Figma Motion and Figma Buzz for locked self-serve templates, Figma Weave for generative image and video, Creative Engine for automated static and video assets, and Runway. You turn them into automated templates and workflows that CRM, performance marketing and partners run themselves, with brand, responsible gaming and compliance rules built in so the output is right by default; you own best-in-class video generation, and train the models that keep generated imagery and video looking like us. The tools you make are run by CRM managers, performance marketers and designers across in-app, CRM and paid. You can build, not just brief. Design judgement decides what gets built.</p> <h3><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Build and execute automated workstreams for teams including CRM, performance marketing, partners and design: template and variant generators, copy-to-layout pipelines, Figma plugins and automation scripts that go from brief to approved asset, connecting the existing stack end to end (design system components into Buzz templates, Weave agent workflows for promo imagery, Creative Engine extended from Markets into CRM and in-app).</li> <li>Own best-in-class video generation: set up and run the generative video pipeline across Weave, Runway and Creative Engine for hooks, variants, start frames and localisations, and decide which tool does what where they overlap.</li> <li>Train and maintain LoRAs and custom models on the Casino visual identity, products, characters and partner assets so generated imagery and video stay on-brand without hand-fixing; retrain when the brand or a partner changes.</li> <li>Encode the Casino visual identity, responsible gaming requirements and market-specific compliance rules into every workstream, so a CRM manager or performance marketer can run it and the output is safe by default: disclaimer and RG messaging legible and correctly placed at every size. Creative approves anything new.</li> <li>Target the highest-volume executions first (CRM banners, in-app promo cards, paid variants) and measure the before and after in hours per asset.</li> <li>Own the tools after launch: fix them when the brand, a regulator or a vendor model changes, and retire what stops working.</li> <li>Work with the Lead Motion & 3D Designer on motion templates and render pipelines, and with the Design Lead on how brand rules translate into constraints.</li> <li>Document what you build so the team can use it without you, and train the people who run it.</li> <li>Present the roadmap and results to Design, Marketing and senior leadership in plain terms.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Hands-on generative AI in production: image and video generation pipelines across tools like Weave, Runway and ComfyUI, LoRA or fine-tune training for brand consistency, prompt and workflow design. Used through their APIs, not only their interfaces.</li> <li>Judgement about AI output: you can evaluate models on quality, cost, licensing and brand risk, set guardrails, handle failure modes, and tell a marketer plainly what a model can and cannot do.</li> <li>5+ years across design and engineering in any mix, with at least 2 building tools other people used in production. You have shipped design work and you have shipped code; we will ask to see both.</li> <li>Working code: Python or JavaScript/TypeScript, REST APIs, Figma plugin development or equivalent, and a track record of shipping something maintainable rather than a prototype.</li> <li>Enough design craft to tell good from bad and to turn a brand guideline into a rule a machine can apply: layout, typography, colour, hierarchy.</li> <li>A portfolio or repo of tools you built, with who used them, what they replaced and what changed as a result.</li> <li>Comfort in a regulated category where some outputs must never ship, and the instinct to design for that.</li> <li>Clear communication with non-technical colleagues, and the patience to train the people who will run what you build.</li> <li>Curiosity about where the tools are going, and a point of view on what we should not automate.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Bonus points</strong></h3> <ul> <li>iGaming, sportsbook or another regulated consumer category.</li> <li>Dynamic creative or creative automation platforms (Celtra, Storyteq, Bannerflow, Creatopy) and a view on where they fall short.</li> <li>Motion and 3D pipeline work: After Effects scripting, Cinema 4D or Blender automation, render or FFmpeg tooling.</li> <li>Internal tools with a lightweight front end (React, Streamlit or similar) that non-engineers adopted.</li> <li>Working alongside CRM, lifecycle or performance marketing teams on high-volume, multi-market output.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Your first 90 days</strong></h3> <p>You'll learn the stack, the brand rules and the three executions where volume hurts most. You'll ship the first automated workstream against one of them, with CRM running it, and show the hours it saved. You'll have a brand LoRA in use and a clear answer to which of Weave and Runway does what.</p> <p>For information about our benefits, please visit <a href="https://benefitsatfanatics.com/">https://benefitsatfanatics.com/</a></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p></p> <p>By submitting your application, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge you have read our <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5ff494b9931735466ce28d5b/t/69de53bde2c02c25e9c38758/1776178110037/Candidate+Privacy+Policy+April+2026.pdf" target="_blank">Candidate Privacy Policy.</a></p> <p><em>Fanatics will never ask candidates for money, banking information, or other sensitive personal information as part of the interview process. description: <h2>About Scale</h2> <p>Scale builds AI systems for decisions that matter. We started out providing the data and evaluation behind many of the world's leading models, and we still work with the major frontier labs on research and post-training. Today we also build full applications: we take an organisation's own data and expertise, forward deploy alongside their teams, and build the systems they come to rely on, powered by the Scale GenAI Platform.</p> <h2>The Role</h2> <p>The UK is making a wholesale shift to AI. The government's AI Opportunities Action Plan set out to "mainline AI into the veins" of the country, and the focus has now moved to delivery: the Incubator for AI (<a href="http://i.AI">i.AI</a>) is shipping tools like the Humphrey suite into departments, a Sovereign AI Unit and AI Growth Zones are being stood up, and civilian departments are under real pressure to move from pilots to production. Scale can play a foundational role in building the reliable AI applications that shift depends on.</p> <p>We're looking for someone to lead that work in central government. This isn’t about staying in the office and managing a team of sales people, its about building the business from the front. You'd own our commercial relationships across civilian departments, starting where the near-term pipeline is strongest: HMRC, DWP, and NHS.</p> <p>This is a critical role reporting directly to our Head of Public Sector, UK. description: <div class="content-intro"><div> <div> <div class="gmail_quote"> <div> <div><span id="m_-113912706363268805m_-2746164444908759431gmail-docs-internal-guid-131e4fb0-7fff-b4e9-ff50-e8cf32449b1b">CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at <a href="https://www.coreweave.com">www.coreweave.com</a>.</span></div> <div> </div> <div>We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.</div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <p> </p></div><h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>The Staff Data Center Security Design Manager owns the end-to-end physical security design process for CoreWeave’s data center and critical infrastructure portfolio, from construction drawings and specifications through standards and consultant oversight. Reporting to the Director, Data Center Security Programs and Strategy this position directs physical security design across multiple simultaneous data center projects in the Europe and Middle East regions, ensuring that access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, perimeter fencing, gates, and related systems are designed to a consistent, defensible, and scalable standard.</p> <p>This Staff Security Design Manager is the technical authority on security design, setting and continuously improving CoreWeave’s design standards and Basis of Design (BOD) documentation, directing the work of external design consultants, and leading cross-functional coordination with Civil, Architectural, Electrical, and ICT disciplines. The role requires a seasoned physical security design professional who can resolve complex, multi-team design risks independently, identify value engineering opportunities that protect CAPEX, and mentor other security design managers in a fast-growing, high-performance environment.</p> <h2><strong>Key Responsibilities:</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Security Design Ownership: </strong>Own the end-to-end security design process including construction drawings, specifications, and standards for physical security systems (access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, perimeter fencing, gates, and more) across multiple simultaneous data center projects in the Americas Region.</li> <li><strong>Standards & Basis of Design: </strong>Drive development and continuous improvement of CoreWeave physical security design standards, Basis of Design (BOD) documents, and template specifications, ensuring they reflect current best practices, emerging technologies, and lessons learned from the field.</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Design Leadership: </strong>Participate in cross-functional design reviews and page turns, coordinating with Civil, Architectural, Electrical, and ICT disciplines to deliver integrated, compliant security designs.</li> <li><strong>Risk & Deficiency Resolution: </strong>Identify, assess, and resolve complex design risks and architectural deficiencies proactively, including those that span multiple teams or regions.</li> <li><strong>Emerging Technology Evaluation: </strong>Evaluate emerging technologies, construction methods, and security measures for applicability to CoreWeave infrastructure, and champion adoption where enhanced customer requirements, ROI, and/or scalability justify it.</li> <li><strong>Value Engineering: </strong>Identify risk-appropriate value engineering opportunities to reduce CAPEX spend.</li> <li><strong>Consultant Management: </strong>Serve as the primary technical point of contact for physical security design consultants, directing their work, reviewing deliverables, and holding them accountable to CoreWeave standards and SLAs.</li> <li><strong>Collaboration & Influence: </strong>Collaborate across CoreWeave Security, DC Design, EHS, and other stakeholders to ensure design outputs align with operational and compliance requirements.</li> <li><strong>Mentorship & Team Development: </strong>Mentor and develop other Physical Security Design Managers, strengthening their technical acumen and design judgment.</li> <li><strong>Construction Reviews: </strong>Conduct construction reviews and design coordination meetings with applicable Security Technical Project Managers responsible for commissioning the security systems..</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Qualifications:</strong></h2> <ul> <li>8+ years of physical security design and/or delivery experience for complex data center or mission-critical infrastructure projects including greenfield owned and leased multi-tenant facility designs.</li> <li>Deep working knowledge of physical security systems design, including access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, perimeter fencing, and gates, and the construction documents and specifications that define them.</li> <li>Proven ability to lead cross-functional design reviews and page turns with Civil, Architectural, Electrical, and ICT disciplines, and to resolve design conflicts that span teams or regions.</li> <li>Experience directing and holding external design consultants accountable to scope, standards, and SLAs.</li> <li>Ability to effectively direct Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to produce high-quality, relevant deliverables at scale.</li> <li>Working knowledge of Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) principles and their application to data center site and facility security design.</li> <li>Ability to travel up to 25%.</li> <li>Relevant certifications preferred (e.g., PSP, CPP, or equivalent physical security design credentials).</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Why CoreWeave?</strong></h2> <p>At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:</p> <ul> <li>Be Curious at Your Core</li> <li>Act Like an Owner</li> <li>Empower Employees</li> <li>Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences</li> <li>Achieve More Together</li> </ul> <p>We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the organization’s growth opportunities are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!</p> <h2><strong>Compensation & Benefits</strong></h2> <p>The starting salary will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility).</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>To fulfill our obligation to protect client data, successful applicants offered employment with CoreWeave will be required to complete a basic criminal record check, conducted in compliance with GDPR. Employment offers are conditional upon receiving satisfactory check results.</em></p> <p><strong>What We Offer</strong></p> <p>In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs, including:</p> <ul> <li>Family-level Medical Insurance</li> <li>Family-level Dental Insurance </li> <li>Generous Pension Contribution </li> <li>Life Assurance at 4x Salary </li> <li>Critical Illness Cover </li> <li>Employee Assistance Programme </li> <li>Tuition Reimbursement</li> <li>Work culture focused on innovative disruption</li> </ul> <p><em>Benefits may vary by location. </em></p> <p><strong>Equal Opportunity </strong></p> <p><em>CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace. title: Product Manager
description: <p> </p> <h2>About Fospha</h2> <p>Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working - across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop - down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on. Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, and Lululemon use Fospha every day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform - and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.</p> <h2>The role</h2> <p>We're hiring two Product Managers to own major parts of the Fospha platform. You'll decide what gets built and why, get it shipped, and prove it worked for clients.</p> <p>This is a role for a doer. You'll own a significant product area end to end, set its direction, and run several initiatives at once. A delivery manager and engineering lead run day-to-day delivery alongside you, so your time goes on the decisions that matter: which client problem to solve, what it's worth, what to cut, and whether what shipped actually moved the needle.</p> <p>You'll join an established team, supporting our continued transformation in a post-AI era. We're looking for people who will push how we structure and execute to maximise the value of Product work, not take their first step into Product management.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Own a product area end to end.</strong> Take initiatives from problem, sizing and discovery through build, launch and adoption. Make the sequencing calls for your area and run several initiatives in parallel.</li> <li><strong>Start every initiative with why.</strong> Before anything is built, be clear on the client problem, the evidence for it, the expected impact for clients, what it's worth commercially, how it fits our pricing and packaging, and how it advances company strategy. Fospha's business strategy hinges on its product strategy, so every initiative should trace back to it. Say no to good ideas that aren't the most important thing.</li> <li><strong>Stay close to clients.</strong> Don't wait to be invited: set up your own client calls as well as joining others', run interviews and prototype sessions, and pair what clients tell you with what the usage data shows. Know what clients see on screen and what they do with it.</li> <li><strong>Decide quickly on imperfect information.</strong> Know when the evidence is strong enough to act, make the call, and change course when the evidence changes, including stopping work that isn't landing.</li> <li><strong>Work AI-first.</strong> Use AI to compress discovery synthesis, analysis, spec writing and stakeholder communication. Build and refine your own agents, workflows and prototypes, and work with engineers on what can be prototyped with AI coding tools. Share what works with other PMs and feed improvements back to Product Ops, so the whole team gets faster.</li> <li><strong>Prove it worked.</strong> Set success thresholds before build starts, check adoption and usage after release, and act on the result. Shipped is not the same as worked.</li> <li><strong>Give people what they need to decide.</strong> Know what information a decision-maker needs at each point, and give them exactly that: a one-line recommendation for an exec, the full detail for an engineer. Present with confidence to senior leaders, internally and at clients.</li> <li><strong>Raise the bar.</strong> Give direct, useful feedback, take it well, and hold your own work to a high standard.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring (must-haves)</h2> <ol> <li><strong>3+ years as a Product Manager, or in an adjacent role with experience you can clearly apply to product management.</strong> Either way, you can point to problems you owned end to end: deciding what to do, getting it delivered, and measuring whether it worked against success criteria set upfront.</li> <li><strong>2+ years making decisions from data yourself</strong> - product analytics (funnels, usage, retention) and commercial data - pulling and checking your own numbers rather than waiting for an analyst.</li> <li><strong>A track record of connecting your work to commercial outcomes.</strong> You've sized opportunities in revenue or retention terms, built business cases, and shaped pricing, packaging or monetisation decisions with commercial teams.</li> <li><strong>Hands-on client experience.</strong> You've run customer discovery, joined sales and account calls, and turned what clients experience into a clear, evidenced problem statement.</li> <li><strong>Confidence in presenting to peers and senior stakeholders.</strong> You're confident making and presenting recommendations to leaders across the business, advocating for data-backed decisions.</li> <li><strong>Deep, everyday use of AI in your work.</strong> You can describe specific workflows, agents or tools you've built or configured, the work they replaced, and how you check their output.</li> </ol> <h2>How you work</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Conscientious.</strong> You close loops, follow through on what you said you'd do, and catch data or quality issues before they reach a client.</li> <li><strong>Relentless about prioritisation.</strong> You can explain why this, why now and what it's worth, and you're comfortable leaving lower-value work undone.</li> <li><strong>Decisive.</strong> You'd rather make a well-reasoned call today than a perfect one next month, and you're open about the assumptions behind it.</li> <li><strong>Analytical.</strong> You break a problem down, work out what would need to be true, and go and find the data to test it.</li> <li><strong>Clear and concise.</strong> You write and present crisply, lead with the recommendation, and cut what the audience doesn't need.</li> <li><strong>Open on feedback.</strong> You give it directly and kindly, ask for it, and act on it.</li> <li><strong>A doer.</strong> You'd rather build a prototype and a short one-pager than write an extensive PRD about one.</li> </ul> <h2>Nice to have</h2> <ul> <li>Product experience within a complicated B2B data platform business.</li> <li>Product experience within marketing or advertising technology.</li> </ul> <h2>Benefits (UK)</h2> <ul> <li>A workplace pension, through Royal London, with Fospha matching your contributions up to 3%</li> <li>A £1,000/year flexible benefits allowance to put towards private medical insurance, dental cover, a health cash plan, gym membership, extra holiday, or a pension top-up - whatever suits you!</li> <li>Access to Wellhub, giving you one membership across gyms, boutique studios, and wellbeing apps</li> <li>25 days' annual leave plus 8 UK bank holidays, an extra day off for your birthday! and more holiday the longer you stay (26 days after 3 years, 27 after 6)</li> <li>Life assurance worth 4x your annual salary, from day one</li> <li>Cycle to Work scheme, plus discounts on everyday spending through our benefits portal - Apple, Tesco, IKEA, M&S, Deliveroo, cinema tickets and more</li> <li>Quarterly one-to-one sessions with a financial adviser, plus access to payroll-deducted loans through Salary Finance</li> <li>Paid volunteering days each year</li> <li>Regular socials, free weekly snacks, and Lunch & Learn events at our Scale Space office, plus access to the wider Blenheim Chalcot community</li> <li>Opportunities to travel - including to our India and North America offices</li> </ul> <p> </p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow
